pages.text: Tupandactylus imperator was a tapejarid pterosaur which lived in the Early Cretaceous of South America, first discovered in the Crato Formation of Brazil. Its binomial name means “emperor Tupâ wing” in reference to the lightning manifestation of the supreme Tupí deity, though it was initially thought to be a species of the related Tapejara. T. navigans is notable for its massive head crest made of fibrous soft tissue supported by 2 bony projections, which was far

larger than in any of its relatives. Like other tapejarids, T. imperator’s skull seems to be more adapted for eating plant material, indicating a more terrestrial inland lifestyle. Some specimens of this species have even preserved pycnofibers with melanosomes, indicating that it may have been colored similarly to birds in life.
